blocks.text: Why PowerPoint for market research analysts on Mac feels slow

Market research analysts often struggle with the administrative side of reporting. You might spend hours cleaning data in Excel or Tableau only to find that formatting the final PowerPoint deck takes just as long. On a Mac, the interface can feel different from the Windows version you used in school. The ribbon layout is similar but the keyboard shortcuts are unique. Many analysts lose time searching through menus for simple alignment tools or image cropping options.
Essential PowerPoint shortcuts for Mac users
Speed comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Stop reaching for the mouse to perform simple tasks. Here are the most important shortcuts for your daily research reporting.

Remember that Mac does not support the Alt key navigation found in Windows. You must rely on the menu bar or the search field at the top of the app. If you ever get stuck, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a specific button is located. Lazur will draw a circle around the item on your screen so you can click it immediately.

Large decks often become unresponsive when they contain too many high resolution images or embedded data objects. As an analyst, you likely work with heavy charts exported from tools like Power BI or Tableau. To keep your presentation smooth, try to compress your images before inserting them. You can also use the Slide Master to manage consistent layouts across your report. This ensures that every slide follows your company branding without needing manual adjustments on every page.

If your presentation starts to lag, check for hidden objects or massive images. Use the Selection Pane to hide layers and see if performance improves. If you are unsure how to find this, ask Lazur to point it out.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps your reporting workflow

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch of your Mac. It is not a plugin, so it does not interfere with your PowerPoint files. Instead, it acts as a personal guide that sees what you see. When you are stuck on a formatting task, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask for help. Lazur can explain how to use the Morph transition or guide you through setting up a complex chart.

Data visualization is the core of your output. Your stakeholders need to understand the insights without reading every data point. Use clean, simple charts. Avoid 3D effects that distort the data. When you need to update your charts with new data, make sure your source file is saved in a consistent location. If you are using linked data, ensure your file paths remain valid to avoid broken links during your presentation.

blocks.text: Accessibility is often overlooked in research reporting. Every image or chart should have alt text. You can add this by right clicking an image and selecting Edit Alt Text. If you need to do this for many slides, keep the Alt Text pane open and move through your slides quickly.

Before you present, run through your slides in Presenter View. This allows you to see your speaker notes and the next slide while your audience only sees the main content. You can find this under the Slide Show tab. If you struggle to find the right settings, just ask Lazur to guide you through the setup.

Writing speaker notes can be tedious. Instead of typing them, use your Mac's dictation features or hold the fn key to have Lazur draft notes for you. This allows you to focus on the narrative while the AI handles the transcription. You can even use this to draft your slide titles based on your research findings.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my PowerPoint files directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit your files. It guides you, points to features, and answers your questions out loud so you can finish the work yourself.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is currently available only for macOS. A Windows version is planned for the future.

faq.question: How do I speed up a slow PowerPoint presentation?
faq.answer: Try compressing your images, removing unnecessary animations, and checking for large embedded objects. You can also use the Selection Pane to identify hidden or heavy elements.

faq.question: What is the best way to move from Windows PowerPoint to Mac?
faq.answer: Learn the key shortcut differences. Most Windows shortcuts use Ctrl, while Mac uses Command. You will also find that some ribbon navigation is different, requiring more mouse interaction.
